So everybody has been talking about how WoD saw a fast spike and drop in subscriptions. The reason why is no mystery: lack of content.   2. VoA is counted as 1 Raid despite being released in 4 wings. So is ICC.
  3. Instances per month is Dungeons + Raids / #months the Xpac was the current one.
  4. I am generously using June 1, 2016 as the expected release date for the next expansion.

Sources:

  1. http://wowwiki.wikia.com/Instances_by_level

WoW subs is too complex topic to run it down to a simple explanation. For me the most likely reasons are not game related cause if they were Blizzard would have figured them out already. I mean they have all the data including the info from players who cared to write why they canceled their sub.

I've seen so many reasons to "why WoW subs are in decline" and they boil down to "what the author of the theory doesn't like personally". I am not saying it's that in this case but this was my experience in various discussions on the topic.

Most people how I know personally that quit the game did it in vast majority due to real life taking the priority and not being able to spend as much time on WoW that WoW requires in order to play at certain level. People I played with mostly are mostly hardcore raiders and hardcore raiders find it hard to go casual. They often prefer to quit. I am not saying this is the main reason. This is the reason known to me personally.

Anyway, I believe there is no 1 major reason for sub decline. There are many reasons and a lot of them boil down to subjective feelings of players. And people differ.

There is one thing many people forget about. People quit WoW always. What was different at the very begining was that many more joined. This has changed in Cataclysm. Now was it because of market saturation (given no other mmo after WoW was even close to the amount of subs might indicate that) or due to lack of easy, entry content for new players at the begining of Cataclysm which started a domino effect of guilds breaking up due to lack of new blood is up for discussion. Tho I am afraid we really lack data in order to go deep enough into the topic.

You cannot look at only 1 aspect as the main reason. That imo is a huge logical mistake.

You make many good points, and I know I am guilty of the "what the author of the theory doesn't like personally" charge. I guess I am just frustrated that this Xpac seems to have shot its load barely 6 months after release.

I know that I quit because there was nothing to do. At first, it was just Bloodmaul Slag Mines that drove me nuts. Then Skyreach. Then Grimrail Depot. Iron docks always was too easy. Back in wrath it took me so much longer to get bored. Even the raid mechanics began to feel boring routine. This was just what I felt like griping about tonight.

I personally have this theory that the more freedom game gives the more boring it feels for some people. WoW nowadays gives you so many choices. But vast majority of those choices are optional for character progression. I myself welcome that a lot cause I like doing things at my own paste. If I feel that I have to do certain things in order to progress my char a get overwhelmed. I think this kind of thing happened at the begining of MoP with dailies. So yeah, Blizzard went too much the other way with dailies but then again I personally enjoyed this new daily model. And I think that Tannan quests are quite good.

As for PvE content. Well, I've embrased the various difficulty model fully and for me untill I clear everything on Mythic the content doesn't end for me. I'm not uber hardcore so it takes time. But then again I do enjoy that time when I have everything cleared and I can focus on some achievements.

I guess WoW is still looking for that balance between too much mandatory content and to little. WotLK felt overwhelming with too many things staying relevant for too long and being mandatory for more serious players. It's a hard task because for every person this sweet point will be somewhere else. For me personally WoD is the best expantion ever in terms I'm having the most fun. There is stuff to do but not too much feels mandatory so I can even make few day breaks and don't feel like I'm staying behind. During Vanilla, TBC and WotLK I felt I had to play to stay relevant. At the end of MoP I've made a month break and enjoyed some Diablo 3 and other things in life appart from WoW :) I was happy with that feeling of completion and still having free time. I feel like that taking a look at all the "Why WoW Subs are in decline" posts in /r/WoW and /v/WoW, and you can find most reasons. Since it isn't one, singular reason. But it's multiple reasons, that come from bad decision making, short and shoddy x-pacs, little content and the casualization of the game. (The casualization I feel has damaged the game, but no doubt has made it accessible to many more otherwise would be players.)

The problem is that many of those "reasons" for some people are the reason they are still playing. I've seen most of those reasons on forums and none of them could ever possibly apply to me.

I also don't like the term "bad decision making". Only because you personally don't like something doesn't mean it's a bad decision. Those several million subscribers are a very diverse group with often quite opposite feelings on how the game should evolve. There is no way Blizzard can make everyone happy. They are trying tho and they are catering to much more people than before.

Also, the casualization is really tricky topic. I personally find the casualization the main reason why the game still exists. Because casualization doesn't mean the game is easier. It means it's more accessible which you admitted is a good thing. There is a lot of challenge in the game. The gameplay (as in class mechanics) is much more demanding than it was in good old days. The hardest content is by miles harder than anything that the game had to offer in times that people claim were harder. The only difference is that things take less time but that doesn't mean they are easier. Blizzard added a lot easy content to the game so it's possible to make the hardest content harder with each expantion while still having something to offer to the majority that isn't interested in those activities. Sure, for some people something will always be missing but that's not something that's easy to solve.

And forums... forums are the vocal minority. Some thoughts are repeated like mantra but that doesn't mean they are true for majority. And well... once Blizzard did listen to that vocal minority that said WoW is too easy... we had Cataclysm which started the sub drops. Since then Blizzard is much more cautious with listening to vocal minorities and since then the sub drop slowed down. The vocal minority is hardly ever right. There is also one more thing - people who are happy with the game, play it. People who are not, complain on the forums. That's why hardly ever hear from those who agree with Blizzard's decisions.

For me personally WoD is the best expantion ever. With the little exception of lack of flying which for me should have been introduced much earlier... gated by an achievement like now but still much earlier. After I've got all the treasures and did all the quests I really don't feel the need to explore anything else. I just want to get fast from point A to point B.

Most people how I know personally that quit the game did it in vast majority due to real life taking the priority and not being able to spend as much time on WoW that WoW requires in order to play at certain level.

I was running into the same thing as you were, my guild was falling apart, everyone unsubbing and almost invariably siting personal reasons. There was stuff going on at work, the kids were too much to handle, etc., but in discussions in the guild forums we actually began realizing that things weren't any busier or hectic or chaotic than they were at points in WotLK and BC. The only difference was that in WotLK and BC, we were enjoying the game, there was a lot to do, things to strive for and goals to achieve. We made time for the game then because we were enjoying ourselves, but now we're not.

We have always been at war with using HTTPS.

The funny part is that Voat's backend design still includes an adversary able to read every single bit of traffic going to the website.
what adversay at backend? care to elaborate?

CloudFlare is able to read every piece of traffic going to and from Voat, since it currently holds Voat's SSL keys and the site is routed through it. Passwords, logins, habits and page visits can read/obtained by CloudFlare. On top of that, CloudFlare has a US presence, meaning it is subject to NSLs which could result (it's probably already happening) in the US government reading users' traffic without any judicial oversight.

Two things can be done:

1) Voat needs to move to keyless SSL, a CloudFlare feature. Traffic still passes through CloudFlare but it is not decrypted until it reaches Voat. Only metadata is left.

2) Avoid CloudFlare and setup own infrastructure

I think OP's post is important. I just noticed the https today for the first time too, but it's because my browser popped an error message that it could not verify the SSL cert for voat.co. The reason for that was that the cert issuer is StartCom, and my browser couldn't verify it either. So, something changed today.

It's going up and down periodically right now for me. I sometimes cannot reach other sites signed by StartCom, such as https://www.linux.com/ either. Is anyone else getting "Cannot verify SSL cert" errors?

http://s27.postimg.org/x0nksz3oj/ssl_voat_error.png
http://s14.postimg.org/gflu7r67l/ssl_voat.png
http://s12.postimg.org/gmz50le4d/ssl_startcom.png

Okay, so I've looked at this a little more, and can replicate it at will. If I use a browser that has both StartCom Class 1 serial 18 and serial 19 certs (what is up with that??!?) then it doesn't happen, but if I use a browser that has only the Class 1 serial 18 cert, then if I visit another site first, such as https://www.linux.com/ it pops the error and invalidates the cert. voat.co won't work after that. If I visit voat.co first and then visit https://www.linux.com/, then it works until I need to open another TCP port 443 connection (such as entering a new post or sitting until the main connection times out). I think someone from Voat needs to go ask the people at StartCom/StartSSL what is up with this; if they invalidated serial 18 as a result of being broken into last year or something.

TL;DR: StartCom/StartSSL has a problem. Voat should replace its SSL cert with one from a different issuer.
